lesson_title: Number Patterns: The Can Pyramid Question
hook_text: 8 rows of cans. Most people answer 8. The question wanted 36. Here's the difference.
clip_script: Picture the pyramid of cans stacked at the supermarket entrance. One can on top. Two in the row below. Then three, then four — every row one can wider than the row above. Eight rows down, the display is finished. How many cans came off the storeroom trolley? Say it while you build: one. Plus two, three. Plus three, six. Plus four, ten. Plus five, fifteen. Plus six, twenty-one. Plus seven, twenty-eight. Plus eight, thirty-six. The eighth row holds 8 cans, but the display holds 36 — read what the question counts.
visual_style: Stop-motion can pyramid assembling row by row with a running counter ticking upward, freezing on 8 versus 36 side by side.
pacing: Rhythmic build with the counter, a beat of silence, punchline lands on 36.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never lose the stacked-rows marks again.
